item.title: Chevron CEO warns Iran conflict has created 'very real' threat to global oil supplies as gas prices climb
item.description: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warns of "very real" risks to oil supply as the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea and Black Sea face growing threats amid Iran conflict.
item.content:encoded:
Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned of "very real" dangers for the global oil industry as tensions escalate in Iran and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities fuel concerns over a potential new shipping crisis.

His comments come as oil prices climb following President Donald Trump’s pause on U.S. strikes against Iran and as Saudi Arabia reportedly builds an international coalition to protect vital shipping routes.

"We now see, not only the Strait of Hormuz, but the Red Sea and the Black Sea have risks and uncertainties. So, some of the challenges have expanded, and the risks to supply are very real," Wirth said during an appearance on "Sunday Morning Futures."

TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

While oil demand remains strong around the world, Wirth said energy markets are "fragile and uncertain" as the U.S. conflict with Iran festers into a sixth month and as global inventories continue to decline.

"The world energy system has been stressed and the need for supplies to markets and customers has never been higher," the Chevron CEO said.

The Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most vital trade routes, is one of the most contentious aspects of the United States conflict with Iran. Traffic has sunk to only a handful of vessels passing through the waterway each day.

Recent Houthi attacks on another vital Middle East shipping route, the Red Sea, have raised fresh concerns about the reliability of that corridor.

STEVE FORBES URGES TRUMP TO KEEP THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ OPEN AT ALL COSTS

"I think the unfortunate thing is that energy assets have been targeted in this conflict. And what that means is it degrades the capacity of the energy system to meet global demand," Wirth said. "And how quickly that comes back will be one of the things that determines when markets actually get back to some sort of a new equilibrium."

"We've seen supply constrained, we've seen damage to infrastructure. And we have new risks that I think will be priced into the market on shipping."

U.S. crude oil is trading at roughly $84 per barrel, while the national average price for a gallon of gasoline stands at $4.09 – nearly $1 higher than the $3.15 average one year ago, according to AAA.

Despite the growing geopolitical uncertainty, Chevron’s production is up 20% year-on-year, with a 5% increase from Q1 to Q2 of 2026. The oil giant also set a record for producing more than 2 million barrels of oil equivalent in one day, an all-time high for the U.S., Wirth said.

TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

Wirth, who said the U.S. has "stepped up" to solve the global oil crisis, told Fox News that Chevron is exploring ways to bypass oil shipping through the Middle East’s vulnerable and unpredictable shipping waterways.

"We are in discussions with Iraq about potentially entering one or two oil fields there," the Chevron CEO said. "Part of those discussions would include a framework that would allow the construction of a pipeline that would go North and then move to the Mediterranean Sea and create a pathway for that production to get to market that would not have to go through the route today, which is through the Strait of Hormuz. "

item.title: Homeowner blames 'militant vegan' for missing milk before camera reveals real thief
item.description: Security camera video captures a young fox trotting up to Gordon Campbell's doorstep near Glasgow, Scotland, and stealing his milk delivery.
item.content:encoded:
After weeks of missing milk deliveries, a homeowner finally caught the thief on camera — and it wasn't who he expected.

Gordon Campbell, 42, who lives near Glasgow, Scotland, set up a security camera after bottles of milk repeatedly disappeared from his doorstep, news agency SWNS reported.

When he checked the footage, he discovered a young fox had been helping itself to the deliveries.

6 JAW-DROPPING FOOD HEISTS THAT CAME BEFORE THE MASSIVE 12-TON KITKAT THEFT

Video shows the animal trotting up the front steps, grabbing a glass bottle of milk in its mouth, knocking it over and carrying it away.

The mystery had been unfolding for about a month, Campbell told SWNS. At first, he suspected a person was responsible.

He even joked that the culprit might have been "a militant vegan" before discovering it was actually a fox.

"I didn't really know exactly who would be doing it," Campbell said. "I thought it was a person or an animal."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"The magpies got the blame for a while, as they're really smart birds, but I was thinking they probably wouldn't have the strength to roll a bottle away."

Determined to solve the mystery, Campbell set up what he described as a "sting" by placing a spare glass bottle filled with milk outside while positioning a camera to capture the culprit.

The plan worked within hours. Just after 2:30 a.m. on July 20, the fox appeared and took the bait.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I just thought it was kind of hilarious that this... cute fox was popping up and taking it away," Campbell said.

"All was forgiven when I saw its big ears and its wee face."

Campbell had been receiving milk deliveries since the COVID-19 pandemic but temporarily stopped the service because of the repeated thefts, opting to buy milk at the grocery store instead, he said.

Now that he knows who's been taking the bottles, Campbell said he may resume the deliveries but plans to leave a protective box outside, so the milk can be stored safely.

The fox wasn't making its first appearance around the family's home.

Just months earlier, Campbell's cat, Bruce, chased another fox away after it tried to get into the house through the cat door.

item.title: How the Cubs unintentionally helped the Dodgers land Tarik Skubal in blockbuster trade deadline move
item.description: The Cubs were among teams pursuing Tarik Skubal, but a former Chicago prospect helped the Dodgers land the back-to-back Cy Young winner instead.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' acquisition of ace pitcher Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers has sent shockwaves through Major League Baseball ahead of Monday's trade deadline.

While Tigers fans are understandably the most bent out of shape over the back-to-back Cy Young winner getting shipped out of town, fans of the Chicago Cubs have to be No. 2 on the list of most-frustrated fan bases.

The Cubs were among the many teams that appeared to have a legitimate chance of acquiring Skubal, especially during the early stages of the trade rumors involving the 29-year-old. Chicago's starting rotation has been decimated by injuries in 2026, but the team has managed to grab hold of the top spot in the National League Wild Card race.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

Adding Skubal, even with the fact that he is expected to hit free agency following the season, could have thrust the Cubs into the conversation as the top contender in the National League to potentially take down the Dodgers in their quest to win three straight World Series.

Instead, the Dodgers got significantly stronger with the postseason fast approaching, and not only did the Cubs fail to land a certified superstar in Skubal, but they inadvertently helped Los Angeles acquire one of the best pitchers in all of baseball.

In exchange for Skubal, the Dodgers dealt prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan, and Brady Smith to Detroit. Hope, the top-rated prospect in the deal, was drafted 11th overall by the Cubs in the 2023 MLB June Amateur Draft before Chicago traded him in 2024 to the Dodgers as part of a deal that moved first baseman Michael Busch to the Windy City.

Busch has been an important, very reliable piece for the Cubs in what is now his third season in Chicago, but it's impossible to ignore how a former prospect with the Cubs helped what is already the best team in baseball get even better by dealing for a pitcher the team was highly interested in.

Insult to injury could be added sooner rather than later as well, with Skubal potentially making his debut for the Dodgers this week in Chicago when the Cubs host LA for a three-game series beginning on Monday.

item.title: At least 72 dead amid mass migrant rush to storm Spanish enclave of Ceuta sparking border crisis
item.description: At least 72 migrants are dead as Spain searches for more victims and a deadly border crossing sparks renewed political tensions across Europe.
item.content:encoded:
At least 72 migrants are dead after a chaotic rush to storm the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, turning one of Europe's latest border crises into a humanitarian disaster that is reigniting debate over immigration across the continent.

Spanish authorities continued searching the waters off Ceuta over the weekend for additional victims after an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 migrants — most of them young men — poured into the tiny Spanish territory in North Africa. Officials said many of the victims drowned while attempting the crossing, while others were killed in a stampede near a breakwater barrier.

The mass crossing unfolded over several days, temporarily increasing Ceuta's population of roughly 84,000 by more than half. By Sunday, many migrants had returned to neighboring Morocco, while others remained in the city or tried to avoid authorities.

SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD

The deaths have intensified the political fight over immigration in Spain and across Europe. Far-right leaders called for tighter border security and the removal of migrants who remained in the enclave.

Santiago Abascal, leader of Spain's nationalist Vox party, visited Ceuta on Sunday and blasted the country's government, calling the migrant influx "an invasion" and accusing officials of failing to protect Spain's borders.

Tensions were also on display Saturday when European Parliament member Alvise Pérez faced angry counterprotesters during a rally in Ceuta. Pérez eventually took shelter inside a nearby bar before police escorted him away.

MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

Many local residents expressed sorrow over the loss of life, even as the political debate intensified.

"It pains me deeply that young people are dying at sea. It's not right that, in the year 2026, women with children as young as two months old should be crossing the sea only to die," Karima Abenaz, a French national in Ceuta with family in Morocco, told Reuters.

"In Morocco, there's food, there's everything we need," she said. "If we don't have a decent job, we should go on strike and demand our rights from the government. We shouldn't be dying at sea. It's not right."

WHITE HOUSE BLASTS SPANISH GOVERNMENT AS THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS SURGE FROM MOROCCO, EMERGENCY REQUEST DENIED

Other local residents said the migrants themselves should not be blamed.

Mohamad Abdelkader Driss, a waiter in Ceuta, told The Associated Press that responsibility lies with the authorities.

"If you open the border, of course everyone comes in, but the young men aren't to blame. The authorities are responsible," he said.

Others said the events had tested Ceuta's reputation as a city where Christian, Muslim, Jewish and Hindu communities have long lived side by side. Some also voiced concerns about security and questioned whether another mass crossing could happen again.

The U.S. State Department on Saturday raised its Travel Advisory for Ceuta to Level 3: Reconsider Travel in response to the surge, warning that the "massive and uncontrolled arrival of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta may lead to unpredictable and dangerous security situations."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trans activists harass, hurl slurs at Sophie Cunningham supporters before Fever game in Minnesota
item.description: Video shows trans activists shouting slurs and getting physical with pro-women supporters outside Target Center ahead of the Indiana Fever game.
item.content:encoded:
Sophie Cunningham’s stance on protecting women’s sports has become a major flash point across the WNBA, and the backlash followed her supporters to Minnesota on Sunday.

Women’s sports advocates gathered peacefully outside Target Center ahead of the Indiana Fever’s game against the Minnesota Lynx, wearing XX-XY Athletics shirts and holding signs with slogans like "Pro-Women, Not Anti-Trans" and "Trust the Science."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It marked the third rally organized in support of Cunningham since the Fever guard publicly said young female athletes "shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

But trans activists gathered nearby were considerably less interested in peaceful disagreement.

Video from outside the arena shows counterprotesters shouting through megaphones, hurling slurs and attempting to rip XX-XY shirts from the hands of Cunningham’s supporters. One man held a fan displaying the word "C—T" over the women’s heads.

At one point, an activist became physical with a supporter, forcing security personnel to intervene.

So much for love and tolerance.

The Minnesota confrontation followed similar scenes surrounding Fever games in Seattle and Portland.

During the first rally in Seattle, two teenage girls later attended the game wearing XX-XY shirts and holding a sign that read, "Thank You Sophie For Speaking Up For Girls." Storm minority owner Celeste Keaton allegedly approached the girls courtside, cursed at them and called them "f—ing insane," leaving one of them in tears.

STORM CO-OWNER SUSPENDED AFTER INCIDENT WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS AS STAR BREAKS SILENCE ON CONTROVERSY

The WNBA subsequently fined the Storm and suspended Keaton from attending the team’s next five home games.

Supporters rallied again Friday outside Portland’s Moda Center, where trans activists interrupted speakers, cursed at reporters and confronted attendees. Inside the arena, Cunningham was relentlessly booed whenever she entered the game or touched the ball.

Cunningham, however, made it clear before the Portland game that she had no intention of backing down.

"I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me," she said. "I’m not going to, like, shadow that or hide or, you know, dim my light just because maybe people don’t agree with that."

item.title: WWE legend Torrie Wilson nearly retired from posting sexy photos after a call from a so-called friend

item.title: Sen Bernie Moreno calls for ex-son-in-law to resign from House, get 'serious psychological help'
item.description: Sen. Bernie Moreno called for Rep. Max Miller's resignation and said his former son-in-law needs psychological help amid domestic abuse allegations.
item.content:encoded:
Unmoved by his former son-in-law's X livestream denials Sunday, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, called on Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, to resign from Congress and seek "serious psychological help."

"If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them," Moreno wrote in a lengthy statement on X. "He should not serve in the House of Representatives."

It was a call repeated by Miller's Democratic challenger in Ohio's 7th Congressional District.

"No one credibly accused of holding a gun to his wife's head and breaking their 2-year-old daughter's collarbone belongs in the halls of power," Brian Poindexter, the union ironworker and Brook Park city councilman, wrote in a statement Sunday.

GOP REP MAX MILLER PUSHES BACK AGAINST ABUSE ALLEGATIONS: ‘I HAVE NOTHING TO HIDE’

Moreno delivered an even more blistering public rebuke an hour after Miller livestreamed a sweeping denial of domestic abuse allegations made by ex-wife Emily Moreno, the daughter of the senator.

"As he has admitted privately, Max Miller needs serious psychological help," Moreno wrote. "He is a danger to my daughter, and I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter."

The aftermath of the couple’s divorce had been "pure hell" for his family, Moreno began.

"As a father and husband, I can tell you the last two years have been pure hell for my wife Bridget, our daughter Emily, me, and our entire family in the aftermath of Emily's divorce," Moreno wrote.

5TH ACCUSER COMES FORWARD AGAINST REP ERIC SWALWELL AHEAD OF EXPECTED RESIGNATION

"It has been horrific to watch this play out in full public view, all while knowing an innocent two-year-old girl is caught in the middle. Our priority has always been protecting our daughter and our granddaughter.

"Out of concern for the safety of my family, I hoped to keep this matter private but Max Miller’s increasingly erratic and dangerous behavior has made that impossible."

Miller has categorically denied abusing Emily Moreno or their daughter. In the livestream, he said no court or government agency had substantiated an allegation of abuse against him and that he had never faced a criminal charge related to the claims.

The congressman said child welfare investigations involving his daughter had been closed without findings against him. He also argued that the allegations emerged as the former couple’s custody battle intensified and accused his former wife of using them as leverage.

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

Emily Moreno has accused Miller of physically assaulting and threatening her during their marriage, including allegedly holding a gun to her head. Questions have also been raised about how the couple’s daughter suffered a broken collarbone. Miller denies causing the injury and said his daughter was no longer in his care when it was discovered.

Miller also denied an allegation that he threw boiling water on his former wife, saying he sprayed her with water from a kitchen sink during what he described as horseplay.

"It is shameful that Max Miller decided to go on a bizarre and lie-filled rant about his ex-wife to desperately try to save his political career," Emily Moreno spokesman Stefan Mychajliw wrote in a statement Sunday.

"There is a documented trove of evidence that Miller has a history of violent and dangerous behavior and no amount of victim shaming will change that. 

"It is despicable and abhorrent that Miller lied on an unhinged and humiliating video for their daughter to watch one day.

"No loving parent would have ever used their daughter as a PR pawn to save their own political career. Miller can lie and spin on X, but he cannot do so under oath in a court of law. We are confident that justice will prevail in court."

The extraordinary intervention from a sitting Republican senator adds pressure on Miller as a Wednesday deadline approaches for the party to replace him on the November ballot. Democrats have increasingly viewed the northeast Ohio district as a possible pickup opportunity amid the controversy.

Miller, a former advisor in President Donald Trump’s first administration who had Trump’s endorsement, insisted Sunday that he would remain the Republican nominee.

"I’m not dropping out of this race," Miller said. "And I’ll win in November."

item.title: Eagles' Cooper DeJean walks out with Morgan Wallen during final stop on 'I'm the Problem' tour
item.description: Cooper DeJean joined Morgan Wallen for his signature walkout at Lincoln Financial Field, sending the Philadelphia crowd into a frenzy on tour's finale.
item.content:encoded:
Morgan Wallen closed out his "I’m the Problem" tour Saturday night with a little help from one of Philadelphia’s newest sports heroes.

Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean joined Wallen for his signature pre-show walkout at Lincoln Financial Field, sending the hometown crowd into a frenzy before the country star ever reached the stage.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

Wallen wore Allen Iverson's Philadelphia 76ers jersey as the two walked toward the stage. But the previous night, Wallen rocked DeJean’s No. 33.

A little foreshadowing, perhaps? Apparently, DeJean had been sitting on the surprise all day.

During Eagles practice earlier Saturday, the All-Pro defensive back was asked how he felt about Wallen wearing his jersey on stage. DeJean called it "sick" and said he is a "huge Morgan Wallen fan."

Then he offered a small hint about what was coming later that night.

"Stay tuned," DeJean said in a video posted by the Eagles on social media.

DeJean has quickly become one of Philadelphia’s most popular athletes after helping the Eagles win Super Bowl LIX then earning First-Team All-Pro honors in 2025.

MORGAN WALLEN AND ELLA LANGLEY'S BALTIMORE PERFORMANCE OF 'I CAN'T LOVE YOU ANYMORE' GOES VIRAL

Celebrity walkouts have become a regular feature of Wallen’s stadium shows, and DeJean is now the latest in a very long line of prominent athletes and sports figures to get the honor.

Peyton Manning, Tom Brady, Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Ray Lewis and Myles Garrett are among the NFL stars who have previously accompanied Wallen. Caitlin Clark, Tyrese Haliburton, Mike Tyson and Connor McDavid have also made appearances.

Yet Clark was somehow the only one who got absolutely skewered for it and labeled a racist by certain corners of the internet.

For some reason.

But I digress.

Saturday’s concert capped a two-night run at Lincoln Financial Field and officially brought Wallen’s massive stadium tour to a close. Brooks & Dunn, Ella Langley, Hudson Westbrook and Blake Whiten were among the supporting acts for the finale.

The end of the tour does not appear to mean Wallen plans on disappearing for long, either.

During a recent show in Ann Arbor, Mich., Wallen told fans he has already been back in the studio working on whatever comes next.

"It’s a little bittersweet because we’re getting close to the end of this tour. Kind of the end of this album’s era, I guess you could say," Wallen said. "I ain’t really sure exactly what I’m gonna do next, but I do know that I’ve been in the studio. I’ve been making a lot of music. I’m excited about it."

New Wallen music coming and the NFL season kicking off in just over a month. It’s a good time to love pop country and football.

item.title: Stephen Baldwin on choosing born-again Christianity over Hollywood after a life-changing encounter with God
item.description: Stephen Baldwin reveals how a Brazilian housekeeper's prophecy and a skateboarding ministry led him to leave Hollywood after finding mega success.
item.content:encoded:
Stephen Baldwin believes he could have been one of Hollywood's biggest stars, but he doesn't regret leaving the business for something far more important: his faith.

In a new interview, Baldwin, 60, reflected on the career-defining success that followed his role in the Oscar-winning 1995 crime thriller, "The Usual Suspects," and opened up about why he never felt drawn to chase stardom.

"I probably could have pointed myself in the direction of becoming a big star," Baldwin told People. "But that wasn't me. I didn't want to be Tom Cruise, and have to make $100 million at the box office. I'd rather be a schmuck from Massapequa."

HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE

Baldwin said his priorities shifted dramatically after embracing born-again Christianity in 2001.

According to the actor, his faith journey began after he and his wife, Kennya, hired a Brazilian housekeeper who claimed she had been sent by God because the couple would one day become Christians and start a ministry.

"My wife tells me, ‘I just spoke to Augusta, and she said the real reason she’s here is because God spoke to her, and she said in the future you and I will become born-again Christians and have our own ministry,’" Baldwin told the outlet.

JD VANCE REVEALS WHAT DREW HIM BACK TO GOD AFTER SEEING CHRISTIANS HAD LIFE ‘FIGURED OUT’

At first, Baldwin admitted he was skeptical. However, after attending a handful of evangelical events with his sister — who had already become a born-again Christian — and witnessing a Christian skateboarding ministry that blended extreme sports with worship, he said everything shifted.

"Down on the beach, they had built a skate park on the sand with plywood. And these funky, super committed, cool, tattooed, pierced skateboarders were there and they’d skate, stop, pick up a microphone and start preaching evangelistically, and like 5,000 kids would be around watching because of their interest in the skateboarders," he recalled. "I felt a calling."

Baldwin eventually created a skate video with a Christian message, titled "Livin' It."

FORMER SUPERMODEL SAYS CELEBRITIES NEED TO 'WAKE UP' AND RECOGNIZE CHRISTIAN FANS

"In the first six months we’d distributed 10,000 copies. Then one of the bigger churches called and asked what it would cost to bring the skaters from the video to their church for a live event. So that’s when I left Hollywood," he said. "I went to 125 churches over four years," he said. "Jesus and the Holy Spirit fascinated me."

Baldwin admitted that Hollywood hasn't always been super accepting of his religious and political outspokenness.

"I think they thought I act a little too weird," said Baldwin, who supported President Donald Trump in 2016 and 2024.

"I get a lot of DMs from people who tell me how my work has touched them and that’s all that matters. I’m happy to be where I’m now at 60. I’m so blessed. And I absolutely believe that the best is yet to come."

Today, Baldwin says he's focused on producing faith-based films for younger audiences while hosting his podcast, "One Bad Movie," where actors discuss the worst film or filming experience of their careers.

The actor also said becoming a grandfather has only strengthened his perspective on life.

"I've done 100 movies, I've made more money than I could have wildly imagined, and I'm married to the hottest chick I've ever seen in my life," Baldwin said. "Jesus is my rock. My wife is my anchor."

item.title: RFK Jr torches CNN anchor Dana Bash for 'press malpractice' over COVID coverage in explosive clash
item.description: RFK Jr. accused Dana Bash of COVID-era media "malpractice" on CNN, saying she failed to challenge public health authorities and punished dissenters.
item.content:encoded:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. accused CNN anchor Dana Bash of COVID-era media malpractice Sunday, saying she failed to challenge public health authorities and helped marginalize dissenters during the pandemic.

"You were part of the problem. There was absolute press malpractice. Your job — your job — is a fierce skepticism toward authority, and you weren’t doing that," Kennedy said on "State of the Union."

"You were beating up on people who were dissenting," the HHS secretary added.

Kennedy leveled the attack after Bash asked how HHS would prepare for another pandemic and tried to move him away from re-litigating the prior federal response.

Bash pushed back, saying she was trying to ask how Kennedy would prevent another public health crisis.

EX-CBS REPORTER CLAIMS QUESTIONING FAUCI GOT HER 'PULLED OFF AIR' DURING COVID PANDEMIC

"I also don’t want to use this interview to allow you to say things that aren’t entirely true," Bash said. "You’re talking about therapeutics. Fine. It is also factually true that the COVID vaccine worked. The COVID vaccine prevented deaths. There is data, upon data, upon data."

CDC and Harvard researchers estimated in 2023 that primary vaccination could have prevented at least 232,000 deaths among unvaccinated U.S. adults.

After Bash acknowledged the frightening nature of the pandemic and said officials made mistakes, Kennedy accused CNN of contributing to public fear.

"You were scaring people," Kennedy said.

INSIDE FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY: WHAT HE WROTE ABOUT TRUMP, TV PERSONALITIES AND CELEBRITIES

Bash asked why he believed CNN had frightened viewers, prompting Kennedy to point to its pandemic chyrons.

"Because that was the job of CNN," Kennedy said.

Bash said the network had been covering government officials, including President Donald Trump's daily White House briefings.

"We were listening to the leaders in this country, including the president, who had a daily press conference explaining what was going on," Bash said.

LEGACY MEDIA COVERS ANTHONY FAUCI DIARY BY CRITICIZING DONALD TRUMP INSTEAD OF FAUCI'S DISHONESTY

CNN defended Bash’s questioning and the network’s pandemic coverage in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Dana Bash is a veteran journalist who conducted a newsmaking interview with Secretary Kennedy in which he stated that he supports parents getting their children vaccinated against measles and addressed President Trump’s push for further study into autism and vaccines," a CNN spokesperson said.

"Asking tough, substantive questions to those in power is the job of every journalist, and Dana did hers incredibly well today. We stand behind Dana, her reporting, and CNN’s overall coverage of the COVID-19 pandemic," the spokesperson added.

Kennedy later accused Bash of punishing people who distrusted Fauci, claiming he lied about masks, social distancing, natural immunity, vaccine transmission and COVID-19's origins.

"We know that Anthony Fauci, who was the expert, was lying about everything," Kennedy said. "He was lying. And you were punishing people for not trusting the experts."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The interview aired four days after Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times on his attorney's advice during a Senate hearing into the pandemic response and COVID-19's origins, Fox News Digital reported. 

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., has said his committee will vote on a contempt resolution.

Bash’s questioning also came as the United States recorded its highest measles total in 35 years. The CDC reported 2,371 confirmed cases through July 30, surpassing 2,289 for all of 2025. Kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% during the 2019-2020 school year to 92.5% during 2024-2025.

When Bash asked Kennedy to tell parents directly to get their children vaccinated, he endorsed the MMR vaccine.

"Parents should get their children vaccinated for measles," Kennedy said. "Measles vaccine is effective. It stops measles in about 97% of the cases. People should get vaccinated."

Bash previously said in April reporters should identify false or misleading claims instead of merely presenting competing positions.

"Objective reporting doesn’t mean just giving all sides of the issue," she said. "Objective reporting now, rightly so, means explaining what somebody says when it’s false or when it’s not right or when it’s misleading."

Fox News Digital reached out to RFK Jr. for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Tom Selleck said he almost missed playing iconic role on 'Magnum, P.I.': 'It was a big fight'
item.description: Tom Selleck reveals James Garner's advice that saved his career and led to a complete rewrite of the original "Magnum, P.I." script he initially hated.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Selleck almost passed up one of his most iconic roles.

During a recent conversation with Ted Danson on his podcast, "Where Everybody Knows Your Name," Selleck explained that a conversation with fellow actor James Garner about his issues with the original script of "Magnum, P.I." ultimately convinced him to take the job.

"I'm sitting there, and I'm pretty preoccupied 'cause something had happened," Selleck told Danson. "And he says, ‘What's wrong?’ And I said, ‘Well, look, I had a contract at the studio for a series, but I fulfilled that contract. Now the studio is assigning this show to me, saying the contract is still valid and that I have to do it.’ The show, incidentally, was called ‘Magnum’ and I hated it. It was terrible."

TOM SELLECK SAYS ‘BLUE BLOODS’ CAST MADE MAJOR SACRIFICE TO SAVE THE SHOW BEFORE CANCELLATION

In the original script, written by Glen A. Larson of "Battlestar Galactica" and "Fall Guy," Thomas Magnum had "no flaws, and he had two beautiful women on his arm and a Ferrari."

Garner advised Selleck, "‘You don't have much power, but if they want you, you'll never have more power than you do right now. That's all I'm gonna say.’ And I said no to the studio. And Jim Garner, in a way, just kind of saved my life. I would've been long gone from that version of ‘Magnum.’"

Selleck has made similar comments in the past – in 2015, he told AARP that the original version of the character was "very James Bond-like."

He referenced Garner then, too, saying that he told the people behind the show that he'd prefer it if the character was more similar to Garner's Jim Rockford on "The Rockford Files."

"I said, 'I don't want to be Rockford, but I want to do something like that, where the guy is fallible,'" he said at the time.

Selleck admitted to Danson that "it was a big fight for a long time," saying that his lawyer later told him that he would have a choice of three submissions for "Magnum, P.I."

By that time, Selleck said he had done a miniseries called "The Sacketts," "which was a huge, huge break. So they knew that I could handle a series. And so, they gave me a choice. ‘And you're gonna meet with these writers.’"

Selleck said he had never met with a writer, "And now the writers are auditioning for me."

He told "Magnum, P.I." co-creator Donald P. Bellisario, "I want to do something like ‘Rockford.’ I want a character with flaws and some heart.’ And he said, ‘Say no more.’ He did. And he came back in about two weeks with the best TV movie I had ever read at the time, and it was called ‘Magnum.’"

Selleck admitted to Charlie Rose in 1997 that he'd "bet the farm" by pushing back so hard on the initial script.

"They said I can’t do that, and I said ‘I know I can’t, but I’m going to, and you’ve got to change this, or I can’t do it,'" he told Rose, adding that "had it not worked out, I think I would have gotten a pretty good reputation for being difficult and never worked again. But the point was I wanted to play a flawed guy."

SCOTT EASTWOOD CREDITS HIS FAMOUS FATHER'S WORK ETHIC FOR MAKING HIM AWARE OF 'BULLS---' IN THE FILM INDUSTRY

The "Blue Bloods" star told Danson he refuses to ever call the show anything but "Magnum" because after the studio lawyers looked at it, they worried Clint Eastwood would sue over the title’s similarity to "Magnum Force," "So, we'll put a P.I. there."

"I did not like that," he said. "But we lost that battle. P.I. in Hawaii is not the most flattering term for Filipino Islander, and I was living in Hawaii at the time, and I just… so I don't call it that name, I call it ‘Magnum.’"

At the time, Selleck said that despite his success with "The Sacketts," he had done six unsold pilots, "and I know what they were saying. They're saying, ‘Who the hell does he think he is? He's never even gotten on the air.’ So, if it hadn't worked, I would've been long gone and back with United Airlines pretty quick."

Selleck had participated in United Airlines’ management training program while studying business in college.

"But, I don't know, it was a risk. I'm not sure my dad ever said, ‘Risk is the price you pay for opportunity,’ but he lived his life that way. And this seemed to me to be the time to take a risk."

item.title: Trump DHS chief under fire from conservatives after immigration speech ignites backlash
item.description: Former Border Patrol Chief Gregory Bovino accused Markwayne Mullin of undermining mass deportations after the DHS secretary called for immigration reform.
item.content:encoded:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is facing a conservative backlash after reaffirming his opposition to amnesty in a social media post, with critics arguing the hardline message contradicted comments he made hours earlier during an immigration speech in Oklahoma.

Hours after speaking at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting in Oklahoma City, Mullin wrote on X: "NO amnesty for illegal aliens. Ever."

"We are a nation of laws," he wrote. "If you are illegally present in the United States of America—you will be detained and deported. Period."

The post did little to quell criticism from some conservatives, who argued it conflicted with remarks Mullin made earlier in the day.

RED STATE GOVERNOR PUMMELED ONLINE AFTER DEFYING TRUMP’S DEPORTATION ORDERS

"Why were you at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting today saying the exact opposite of what you are posting now?" one user wrote on X. "Did you suddenly radically change your mind about America's immigration policy in the past couple of hours? Or are you a liar?"

Former Border Patrol Chief Gregory Bovino also criticized Mullin's remarks, writing on X that "Voters asked for mass deportations. Clear demand. High priority. No ambiguity." He added, "The guy running DHS is making the case for 'immigration reform.' We've seen this script before."

In a separate post, Bovino wrote that Mullin had delivered "a masterclass in how to give terrible answers during a single interview" and argued, "Now you know why we're not getting mass deportations."

Conservative commentator Robby Starbuck also weighed in, calling Mullin's remarks "a total betrayal."

During the event, Mullin argued the U.S. needs immigration reform, distinguished between immigrants pursuing legal status and those who are not, and called for changes to some employment visa programs to address labor shortages.

"We haven't had actual immigration reform since 1959. There's a reason. It's political," Mullin said. "Do you really need immigration reform? Yes, you do."

BIDEN ADMINISTRATION FORCED A FALSE CHOICE ON AMERICANS ABOUT IMMIGRATION

Mullin also argued the country should modernize some employment visa programs.

"If we're looking to grow our economy, then we need to look at making more permanent solutions," he said, adding that "there's a way to utilize labor where we're not having the participation rate we need to... and we can plug those holes."

At the same time, Mullin repeatedly emphasized that immigration laws must be enforced.

"If you have a criminal background, we're not making exceptions for you," he said. "There are zero exceptions."

Mullin added that immigrants who entered the country illegally or overstayed their visas without pursuing legal status could not expect relief.

"There's nothing I can do for you," he said.

The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Mayor calls upscale restaurant bombing a 'brutal terrorist act' after 3 killed, 21 injured
item.description: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin vowed to hunt down those responsible after a body-worn bomb detonated at an upscale restaurant on Saturday killing three.
item.content:encoded:
A bombing at an upscale restaurant in Moscow that killed three people and wounded at least 21 others on Saturday was a "brutal terrorist act," according to the city’s mayor, who vowed to hunt down those responsible for the attack.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin made the declaration Sunday, a day after the explosion tore through the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant in the Russian capital.

"Yesterday, a brutal terrorist act was committed in Moscow that claimed human lives. The victims are currently in the city’s hospitals, where they are receiving all necessary care," Sobyanin wrote on social media Sunday.

EXPLOSION AT RESTAURANT IN CENTRAL MOSCOW LEAVES THREE DEAD, MORE THAN A DOZEN INJURED

He added investigators are working to identify those behind the attack and vowed they "will certainly be found and will face the punishment they deserve."

Russian authorities have not identified any suspects, and no group had claimed responsibility as of Sunday.

Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee said the blast was caused by a homemade explosive device. Russian state news agency RIA Novosti, citing local officials, reported that a woman carrying the bomb tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard before it exploded.

The blast killed the woman, the security guard and a restaurant patron, RIA Novosti reported. At least 21 other people were injured in the explosion, which happened around 8 p.m. local time at the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square.

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

The restaurant was closed to the public Saturday night for a private event, according to its website and Russian state media.

Video released by Russian state media showed heavily armed police officers, ambulances and other emergency vehicles outside the damaged restaurant as investigators examined the scene.

Earlier this year, Russia's Federal Security Service, or FSB, said it would tighten security for senior military and government officials following a series of assassination attempts in Russian cities since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Russian authorities have not linked the restaurant bombing to those earlier attacks or to the war in Ukraine.

Fox News Digital’s Brie Stimson and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Bryan Kohberger's former defense expert calls for death penalty, says investigators missed key evidence
item.description: A defense expert hired by Bryan Kohberger now says cellphone data shows evidence of stalking, contradicting his own earlier expert report in the case.
item.content:encoded:
Admitted Idaho murderer Bryan Kohberger should get a new trial and face the death penalty, according to a digital forensics expert hired by the defense who says investigators missed damning evidence against the 30-year-old former criminology PhD student — although his own expert report for the case appears to contradict some of the claims.

Sy Ray is a former Arizona homicide investigator who is now an expert on digital forensics, geolocation and similar data. Kohberger's lawyers hired him as an expert witness for the defense before Kohberger pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty for the home invasion murders of Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Madison Mogen, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, also 20.

Kohberger, now serving four consecutive sentences of life in prison without parole, petitioned the court last week to withdraw his guilty plea and seek post-conviction relief, which could send the case to trial — and put the potential death penalty back in play.

KOHBERGER DEFENSE EXPERT WANTS HIS LAWYERS UNDER OATH AFTER KILLER CITES FINDINGS IN BID TO UNDO GUILTY PLEA

"Bring back the death penalty," Ray told journalist Brian Entin in a new podcast. "I am all for this."

He said he is confident that Kohberger would be convicted and claimed that Kohberger's smartphone data is much more incriminating than was revealed previously when police and the courts unsealed thousands of pages of evidence in the case.

"I 100% believe that the offender, who is Bryan Kohberger — there’s no alternative theory in my head at this point," Ray said in the 82-minute episode, which also included Goncalves’ parents, Kristi and Steve, and her older sister, Alivea. "I 100% believe he’s been in the house before."

BRYAN KOHBERGER'S CHOICE OF 'A HOUSE FULL OF WOMEN' MAY HOLD THE KEY TO THE IDAHO MURDERS' BIGGEST MYSTERY

Ray has not responded to attempts to reach him or shared details of his recent claims with Fox News Digital.

Ray claimed that the evidence he reviewed shows Kohberger potentially inside the victims’ home, and at other places when they were present prior to the murders — something that both contradicts his own expert report from January 2025 and that even prosecutors haven’t publicly alleged.

"If you look at those precise measurements, there’s probably five that land directly on what would be the living room of the house," Ray told Entin. "Like the latitude-longitude is the physical house itself, and if you put the house back on the map, and you map those, the hits are inside the house."

IDAHO MURDERS: NEW BOOK ON KOHBERGER REVEALS PREVIOUSLY UNSEEN EVIDENCE, CLAIMS SHEATH COULD BE INADMISSIBLE

"I just want to make sure I understand correctly… because I haven't heard this before — so you're saying, based on the data you saw, the latitude-longitude for Bryan Kohberger’s Samsung was in the living room?" Entin asked.

"The AT&T-derived latitude-longitude from the AT&T’s network that it estimates a location, it lands in the house — and it's a 25-meter range, so we're talking 75 feet, so it could be anywhere in the house on any floor," Ray said. "It could technically be outside the house, it could [be] on the property, but it's showing in the immediate area. My personal opinion is when I look at those, and I map what's happening before and after and I'm looking at all the other evidence. I think these are accurate locations."

That runs contrary to the expert report under his name included in a defense filing from Jan. 23, 2025.

SEND US A TIP

"It is my opinion that the geolocation data I have been provided as of the writing this report does not provide any evidence of association between Mr. Kohberger and any of the decedents and/or Mr. Kohberger’s or decedent’s residence," he wrote.

Still, Ray told the podcast his theory is that Mogen was Kohberger’s primary target due to the number of times he could trace their phones to similar locations.

"I believe Maddie was the target," he said, adding that repeated "collisions" between their phones placed them in roughly the same area at the same time, including at a Pullman party the first week of school and at the A&W store near the King Road crime scene.

He also flagged what he described as Kohberger’s broader "pattern of life," pointing to evidence of stalking before the murders.

That also contradicts his report.

GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB

"I am unable to locate any period of time between June 23, 2022 and November 13, 2022 where Mr. Kohberger’s mobile device is in the same specific area as any of the deceased’s mobile devices," he wrote.

The discrepancy raised red flags for some experts who have been following the case, including Morgan Wright, the CEO and founder of the National Center for Open and Unsolved Cases and the host of "Crime: Reconstructed."

That pattern of life was also broken on the night of the murders, when Ray said he believes the plan to target Mogen went awry and resulted in him fleeing south, where he’d never driven before.

While prosecutors alleged that Kohberger had visited the crime scene a dozen times before the murders and at least once the morning after, they have not pointed to "collisions" with any of the victims the way Ray described in the podcast. In a news briefing after Kohberger's guilty plea, the case's lead investigators said they didn't know who the target was.

"The evidence suggested that there was a reason that this particular house was chosen," said then-Moscow Police Cpl. Brett Payne. "What that reason is, we don't know. We don't know who the target was, and we're not going to speculate on that up here today. But we can tell you that, for whatever reason, Mr. Kohberger chose that residence. Perhaps it's the location, layout, we do not know."

And when they were asked by Fox News Digital if they had a motive, lead investigators replied, "We don't."

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

On Entin's podcast, Ray alleged that they missed the evidence.

"They didn’t even look at it," Ray said of the stalking evidence. "It’s incredible to me."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

However, in Ray's report, he wrote that he "can find no evidence of stalking behavior or surveillance at the King Road Residence," Wright noted.

"This is the sharpest contradiction," Wright told Fox News Digital. "The state's search warrant sought records specifically to determine whether Kohberger 'stalked' any victim or 'conducted surveillance on the King Road Residence.'"

After Kohberger’s guilty plea, Ray said he offered to do a debrief with the FBI to show the evidence he said he found and they missed. He said he got no response, but added that he has presented before hundreds of law enforcement agencies around the country going back to November, he said.

Last week, Kohberger filed a petition for post-conviction relief, claiming he had ineffective counsel from his defense team.

Ray also speculated that Kohberger’s post-conviction petition was part of a broader legal strategy by his lead defense attorney Anne Taylor despite the plea agreement’s waiver of most appeal rights.

Kohberger pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty.

"This can never be the standard investigation that we see in cases," Ray said. "This can never be acceptable."

However, he said he’s confident Kohberger would be convicted anyway at trial — if investigators introduced the evidence he found while working with Taylor.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"The time is now to start this investigation over," Ray said.

Kohberger had followed other people in the Moscow-Pullman area, he said — a pair of college towns on the border of Washington and Idaho.

"I think he had multiple targets throughout the entire Moscow-Pullman area," Ray said. "Location information and pattern of life is by far the most telling."

Ray said he has no doubt that Kohberger committed the murders.

"If he ever does walk, he will kill again," he said.

item.title: Lifeguards save young boy, 5 years old, as he's pulled unconscious from ocean
item.description: Two lifeguards working at Silver Beach, in Volusia County, Florida, are responsible for rescuing a young child who was pulled unconscious from the ocean during a summer trip.
item.content:encoded:
Another dramatic rescue of a young life has taken place this summer as strong ocean waves and powerful tides continue to prove challenging for vacationers and travelers.

Two lifeguards at Silver Beach in Volusia County, Florida, are being credited with lifesaving action on July 30. 

Lifeguard Dempsey Manhart was just about to take his lunch break, he said, when the family of a young child flagged him down, frantically waving for help, as FOX 35 Orlando reported.

CALIFORNIA LIFEGUARD SPEAKS OUT ON HEARTSTOPPING OCEAN RESCUE: ‘I LOVE WHAT I DO’ 

The boy was unconscious and was being held in the arms of a family member, Manhart recalled. 

He began helping to bring the boy in from the water when his co-lifeguard, Mackenzie Malone, arrived beside him and checked the boy’s pulse — at which point the lifeguards immediately began CPR on the child. 

Malone, who's been working as a lifeguard for her fourth summer, told FOX 35 this was the first time she experienced saving a child from drowning. 

"We’re always expecting anything," she said. "We’re always prepared. We always make sure that we know what to do no matter what the scenario is."

She said the moment her co-lifeguard shouted to her that he was going on a rescue, "I knew that it was going to be serious."

Then everything kicked up a notch. 

"The moment I saw that [the child] was unconscious, that he had a wound on his head … I knew that it was going to be something big." 

The duo began performing CPR on the child.

In short order, he began breathing on his own again. 

Malone later said her lifeguarding and life-saving training kicked in. 

"Thankfully, it ended up in a positive direction," she told FOX 35. "I’m just very grateful that [with] everything we followed, it worked out and that [the boy] actually is able to have a life and come home to a family." 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The lifeguards said they hope the rescue of the child provides a reminder for beachgoers to swim near staffed lifeguard towers — where trained responders can provide immediate assistance in an emergency.

"Heroes!! I am grateful to learn just how well-trained beach lifeguards are," wrote a Facebook user about the Florida beach rescue. 

Volusia County is about 50 miles northeast of Orlando, in the east-central region of Florida. 

"God bless their strength," wrote another person. 

The rescue of the 5-year-old boy comes shortly after the heroic rescue of another child, this one by 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams in Santa Cruz, California. Williams braved pounding surf and massive waves to bring a struggling 10-year-old boy safely back to shore, as Fox News Digital reported. 

President Donald Trump has invited the teen lifeguard to the White House to celebrate his brave actions. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Fox News Digital previously reported that Los Angeles County lifeguards performed nearly 2,000 ocean rescues during a single weekend this summer as elevated surf and dangerous rip currents swept Southern California beaches. 

Officials have encouraged visitors to speak with lifeguards about ocean conditions before entering the water.

Swimmers caught in a rip current are advised not to fight it. 

Instead, they should remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until they escape the current, then angle back toward shore, according to the National Weather Service.

Those who cannot escape should float or tread water and signal for help.

Andrea Margolis of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Princess Margaret, Lord Snowdon's country retreat on the market for first time in history at $5.3 million
item.description: Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon's former getaway in the countryside is on the market publicly, for the first time in its over 500 year history.
item.content:encoded:
The former home of Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones, better known as Lord Snowdon's former country retreat, is on the market for the first time in the home's history.

Known as The Old House, the home, which was gifted to Lord Snowdon by his uncle, designer Oliver Messel, prior to his marriage to Princess Margaret, is listed with Blue Book Agency for about $5.3 million.

Originally built in 1481, the cottage in West Sussex came into the possession of the Messel family in 1890 and was passed down for generations before Oliver gifted it to the royal couple.

Upon receiving the 5,750-square-foot home on the 5.52-acre property, Lord Snowdon transformed the dilapidated home into a private retreat away from the public, often hosting many famous faces, including actor Peter Sellers, ballerina Dame Margot Fonteyn, Bianca Jagger, financier Sir Evelyn de Rothschild and more.

PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE’S $3 MILLION FROGMORE MAKEOVER COULD SOON BE ERASED: EXPERTS

"What Lord Snowdon created here was not simply a private home but an extraordinary creative retreat," Theo James-Wright, director at Blue Book Agency, said. "This was a place where royalty mixed with artists, actors, writers and designers, where some of the most influential figures of the 20th century gathered behind closed doors. Very few houses can genuinely claim to have witnessed such a remarkable chapter of British cultural history."

The rich history surrounding this house inspired an episode in season three of the popular Netflix series, "The Crown."

Some of the elements Snowdon brought to the home include a redesigned kitchen, a balcony salvaged from Ascot Racecourse's Royal Box during refurbishment works, a lake he created and a "time capsule of royal, cultural and family life" made up of newspaper clippings detailing royal scandals and major events, put together by Snowdon himself.

The estate features a main house with six bedrooms, as well as a pool house which can be used as a guest suite. In addition, the grounds include a garden office, library, tractor shed and other amenities.

While this is the first time the home has been put on the market publicly, Snowdon did sell it privately in 2003, and the current owners purchased it off-market in 2005.

KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS

"The fact that this is the first time the property has ever been publicly offered for sale makes this a genuinely rare moment," James-Wright said. "Opportunities to acquire houses with this level of provenance, architectural significance and cultural importance simply do not come along very often."

Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon first met in 1958, and their friendship quickly turned into a romance, with the palace announcing their engagement in February 1960.

They were married just a few months later in May 1960 at Westminster Abbey. Their wedding was the first royal wedding to be televised, attracting an estimated 300 million viewers worldwide.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Over the course of their marriage, the couple welcomed two children: their son David Armstrong-Jones in November 1961, and their daughter Lady Sarah Chatto in May 1964.

They were married for 16 years before announcing their separation in March 1976, later finalizing their divorce in July 1978. Despite ending their marriage, the two are said to have remained good friends in the following years.

Following their divorce, Lord Snowdon married Lucy Lindsay-Hogg in 1978, while Princess Margaret never remarried.

Princess Margaret died in February 2002 at the age of 71 due to a stroke, after her health began to decline in the 1990s. Lord Snowdon died in January 2017 at the age of 86.

item.title: Why the Orioles at +118 could be the play against Zack Wheeler and the struggling Phillies
item.description: Zack Wheeler takes the mound for the Phillies against Kyle Bradish and the Orioles as both struggling teams battle for wild card positioning.
item.content:encoded:
Well, the trade market is finally coming to a simmer. Perhaps we can call it a boil after yesterday’s blockbuster. We had two major pitchers traded to teams yesterday, with Luis Castillo (in a down year) going from the Mariners to the White Sox, and, of course, Tarik Skubal heading to the Dodgers.

Maybe we should just call the baseball season now and give them their third straight trophy. Two other teams to keep an eye on take each other on today as the Phillies and Orioles square off.

The Philadelphia Phillies are floundering quite a bit. This has been a unique season where we saw them fire their manager after a few weeks of poor play to start the year. That was a move that probably should’ve been done in the offseason anyway. Then they were arguably the best team in baseball for a month or two. Now, they are just five games above .500 and likely going to be wrapped up in a wild card race for the remainder of the season.

The Phillies don’t have a ton of trade resources, but they also don’t need much more than maybe another bat and a better back-end starter. Their front of the rotation is solid with Zack Wheeler and Christopher Sanchez. Wheeler is 10-2 for the season with a 2.53 ERA and a 0.92 WHIP, one of the best pitchers in the game. He did have a couple of tough starts in July, but he also had three quality outings. The Orioles are hitting .250 against Wheeler in 68 at-bats.

The Baltimore Orioles are also struggling, but they’ve pretty much been the same for the entire year. They are three games under .500, but they’ve never seemed to be a team that was going very far.

The thing is, the Orioles have the talent, but some years it just doesn’t click. It appears to be that type of season for Baltimore. Gunner Henderson isn’t having a great season with a .220 average, but he can’t be the sole person to blame for all of this.

I’d point to the pitching and their rotation, as they are really not a very deep squad. They have some good arms, and their bullpen has been much better lately, but they don’t really have a lock-down starter. Maybe the closest is today’s starter, Kyle Bradish. I took him in his last outing, and it was a disaster.

The Tigers jumped on him for 10 hits and five earned runs over 4.2 innings. Phillies hitters have struggled against him over 32 at-bats with a .188 batting average.

Maybe I'm foolish to do this, but I'm going to go against Wheeler. The Orioles are playing slightly better baseball than the Phillies. They both need this game to help with some momentum and to win the series. Wheeler isn't likely to give up a ton of runs, but I think Bradish will bounce back in this outing. The money has come in on the Phillies a bit, but I think that is mostly people just looking at Wheeler and not the full pitcher. Give me the Orioles at +118.

item.title: Kelsey Plum heads to Phoenix Mercury in blockbuster deal hours before WNBA trade deadline
item.description: Kelsey Plum joins the Phoenix Mercury in a blockbuster WNBA trade deadline deal that sent draft picks back to the Los Angeles Sparks late Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Kelsey Plum is headed to Phoenix.

The Los Angeles Sparks traded the five-time All-Star guard to the Phoenix Mercury late Saturday night in exchange for Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The blockbuster deal came just hours before Sunday afternoon’s WNBA trade deadline and sent the biggest available name on the market to a Mercury team trying to make another postseason run.

Plum, a two-time WNBA champion, has not played since June 21 because of a lower left leg injury. She was expected to return Sunday against the Portland Fire on a minutes restriction, though it is not yet clear whether she will be available when Phoenix visits the Chicago Sky on Monday.

The 31-year-old was putting together one of the best statistical seasons of her career before the injury. Plum is averaging 23.9 points and 6.4 assists through 12 games — both career highs — and led the league in scoring earlier this season.

Her time in Los Angeles lasted only a season and a half.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The Sparks acquired Plum before the 2025 season in exchange for the No. 2 overall pick, hoping the veteran guard could help accelerate a rebuild centered around Cameron Brink and Rickea Jackson. Seattle eventually used that selection on Dominique Malonga, who became an All-Star in her second season.

But the gamble never produced the turnaround Los Angeles envisioned.

The Sparks missed the playoffs in 2025 and currently sit at 10-17 after losing six straight games. They have gone just 2-9 during Plum’s latest absence and are in danger of missing the postseason for a sixth consecutive year.

MERCURY'S NOW-DELETED SOCIAL MEDIA POST MOCKING CAITLIN CLARK DRAWS SCRUTINY AFTER STAR'S INJURY

Los Angeles also parted ways with general manager Raegan Pebley in July, leaving assistant general managers Zach Knowlton and Nate Nielsen in charge on an interim basis.

Plum was set to become a free agent after the season and reportedly did not plan to re-sign with the Sparks, making her the league’s most prominent trade candidate ahead of the deadline. The New York Liberty and Atlanta Dream had also shown interest.

Instead, she lands with a Phoenix team that appears determined to keep pushing forward despite its own disappointing record. The Mercury are 11-19 and six games behind the eighth-place Liberty for the final playoff spot.

So Plum has her work cut out for her.

She should immediately provide Phoenix with another proven scorer, secondary playmaker and championship-tested guard. She could also take some of the offensive burden away from Alyssa Thomas, who leads the Mercury with 8.3 assists per game.

The move marks only the fourth time in WNBA history that an All-Star has been traded during the season.

item.title: Rubio warns Cuba has infiltrated US with spies, calls communist regime an 'espionage superpower'
