His comments follow the State Department’s recent release of a 100-page report detailing Cuba’s influence operations in the U.S., linking the nation to Antifa and radical activism while labeling it the "capital of 21st-century communism."

CUBA BUILT COVERT NETWORK INSIDE AMERICA THROUGH SPIES, ACTIVISTS AND UNIVERSITIES, STATE DEPT ALLEGES

"They actually are an influence and espionage superpower," Rubio said. "If you look at the history of espionage in the United States, Cuba is the only country that consistently has implanted and embedded spies in our system without even paying them," he said.

"We had… a U.S. ambassador, who ended up being a Cuban spy and was recently convicted," he continued. "We've had them penetrate the highest levels of Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)."

Former U.S. ambassador and national security official Manuel Rocha pleaded guilty to and was sentenced to 15 years in prison for acting as a secret agent for Cuba for decades.

US COUNTERINTELLIGENCE ‘WAY BEHIND,’ POST-9/11 RECORD ‘EXTRAORDINARILY NEGLIGENT’, FMR TRUMP WH OFFICIAL WARNS

Rubio said Ana Belén Montes, a DIA analyst who was found passing American secrets to Cuba, represents one of the "single biggest intelligence failures" and potentially the most serious penetration in U.S. history.

The secretary also told Fox News that Cuba employs networks of protesters across the country to advocate for different causes in an effort to pressure U.S. lawmakers.

The secretary claimed that pro-Hamas, anti-ICE and pro-Maduro protests are all linked to the same network of Cuban-hired protesters.

"There's nothing organic about it. It is funded, it is organized and Cuba is a part of that network and in some cases a critical part of the network," Rubio said.

US BASES, ICE FACILITIES TARGETED IN CUBA-LINKED 24-HOUR ACTIVIST MOBILIZATION PLAN

"And it's a network they will weaponize against us," he continued. "And they talk about it openly, about how they will use that network to pressure American policymakers."

Rubio also accused Cuba of running dangerous influence campaigns throughout Latin America.

"If you look all throughout Latin America, every communist left-wing insurgency that's destabilized governments across the region, every single one of them over the last 40, 50 years has found its support, its help, in many cases, its birth, from a Cuban influence operation," the secretary said.

Critics of the State Department’s report suggest the report chronicling how Cuba poses a threat to the United States is a scare tactic to potentially justify U.S. military action against the country.

Rubio dismissed Americans who sympathize with Cuba’s one-party communist republic led by President Miguel Díaz-Canel.

"I know there are plenty of people in American academia and, frankly, in American press that sympathize with the Cuban regime and have for a very long time," he said. "Part of it is motivated by their anti-Americanism and part of it motivated by ideological affinity."

"But it doesn't mean we can ignore this threat," he warned.

item.title: GOP Rep Max Miller pushes back against abuse allegations: ‘I have nothing to hide’
item.description: Ohio Rep. Max Miller went live on X Sunday morning to address and deny allegations made by his ex-wife that he previously abused her and their daughter.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, went live on X on Sunday morning, denying allegations from his ex-wife that he abused her and their daughter.

"I'm not getting out of this race, and I'm winning in November," Miller said at the end of a roughly 17-minute X livestream statement with pictures of his family in the background.

Miller claimed his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, the daughter of Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, has documented mental health circumstances that might have led to her allegations after their public divorce.

"They frame me as an abuser," Miller said, adding there is "no evidence" against him.

GOP LAWMAKER UNDER HOUSE ETHICS REVIEW BLASTS 'BASELESS' INVESTIGATION

"No court or agency has even substantiated any allegation against me," he added. "Every single one of these allegations were already investigated. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me."

Miller released troves of evidence via Dropbox that he says undermines the allegations against him.

"I have nothing to hide," he said.

Faced with a narrow path to winning control of the U.S. House, Democrats are seeing fresh opportunity in a northeast Ohio congressional seat where the Republican incumbent is facing mounting pressure over allegations that he abused his ex-wife and daughter in a bitter and drawn-out dispute with his former spouse.

Allegations against Miller, a White House advisor during President Donald Trump's first term, have been public for years but have recently drawn increased media scrutiny amid an escalating legal back-and-forth with his ex-wife. That has Democrats sensing Miller could be vulnerable in a district he won two years ago with just over 51% of the vote.

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

Over the past week, they have called for Miller to resign, requested a congressional ethics investigation and suggested more help could be directed in the fall toward his Democratic opponent, union ironworker Brian Poindexter. Miller has denied the abuse allegations and filed defamation lawsuits against his ex-wife and a second accuser.

After Miller's X livestream, Sen. Bernie Moreno stood by his daughter's allegations and called for Miller to resign and get "serious psychological help."

"Out of concern for the safety of my family, I hoped to keep this matter private but Max Miller’s increasingly erratic and dangerous behavior has made that impossible," Moreno wrote. "As he has admitted privately, Max Miller needs serious psychological help. He is a danger to my daughter, and I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter.

"If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them.

"He should not serve in the House of Representatives. I believe Max Miller needs to seek professional help to end the clear pattern of abuse he has left in his wake. I believe he should not be free to continue endangering others until he does."

The deadline to resign and be replaced on the November ballot is Wednesday.

Miller addressed the accusations directly Sunday after concluding that traditional media interviews would not allow him to present his full account. He accused reporters of accepting allegations as fact without adequately examining court records, child welfare findings and communications between him and his former wife, Emily Moreno.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: TLAIB FORCES RARE HOUSE PROCEDURE AFTER REPUBLICAN ACCUSES HER OF DEFENDING TERRORISTS

Moreno alleged that Miller threw her against a wall, held a gun to her head and threw hot water on her.

Miller's livestream addressed each of those allegations directly, rebutting each.

"She didn't call the police after that," Miller said of the assault allegation. "She didn't go to the hospital. Ladies and gentlemen, do you want to know what she did? She went straight to a child's birthday party."

On the holding a gun to her head, Miller rejected it on the basis that no criminal account has been made of that serious crime.

"She has also claimed I held a gun to her head while standing over our child because a light wasn't turned off: That never happened," Miller said. "It is absolutely outrageous. And two days after that allegedly occurred, ladies and gentlemen, she asked me to come over for dinner and to stay the night."

Miller added the Dropbox documents — paid for by Miller and produced by his lawyers, he wrote on X after their release — provide that evidence.

SENATOR’S F-BOMB BASHING OF FAUCI ROCKS INTERNET: ‘HIGH-HEAT FASTBALL!’

"I can literally walk you all through this," he continued in the livestream. "These are incredibly serious criminal accusations. And if these accusations were true, I would be in jail.

"My former wife would not have been offering to cook me dinner and inviting me to playgrounds. Think about that."

The hot water incident reported in the media was just "horseplay," according to Miller.

"Now, the boiling water story the media has run with: That story is about an incident in June of 2024 while we were still married, and here's the truth — and this is the absolute truth: It was horseplay in our kitchen," he said "I sprayed water at her from the sprayer attached to our kitchen sink. Tap water, which does not reach boiling temperature or scalding.

"From that day, you could even see my text messages from that day show she was laughing during it. She never sought or received any medical attention ever. And it was two months after this incident, that Oct. 7 recording that she told me I was a very kind person who she didn't think would ever hurt her physically.

"I mean, ladies and gentlemen, this doesn't add up. Our court-appointed parent coordinator testified under oath that the single photo she was shown of this supposed industrial injury looked a little red, and that there was no physician's report. None."

Miller has not been charged with a crime, and records released through court proceedings showed that child welfare authorities did not substantiate several allegations that he abused his daughter.

"Let me begin with the most painful accusation of all: I have never abused our daughter," he began. "Before I go through the facts with you today, understand one thing: Every one of these allegations traces back to a single source, my former wife.

"I filed for divorce in August of 2024. That October, she admitted under oath that I had never harmed our daughter. Every accusation has come since.

"So ask yourself, what is continuing to change?

"Not the facts. There's never been evidence of any kind. What changed, ladies and gentlemen, were the stakes."

Miller said a January 2025 report accusing him of physically abusing his daughter was closed as unsubstantiated that March. He said investigators instead substantiated findings involving two workers at a daycare the child attended.

He also addressed a February 2026 report concerning his daughter’s broken collarbone. Miller said the injury was discovered after he had returned the child to Moreno and that he canceled a planned trip to Florida after learning she had been hurt. According to Miller, authorities closed that investigation in April without substantiating abuse by him.

Miller further described a recent emergency-room visit prompted by what Moreno believed was a bruise on the child’s neck. Miller said the mark was left during finger painting. He also recounted an occasion when Moreno called police over concerns about his daughter’s car seat, saying responding officers determined that the seat had been installed properly.

The Associated Press reported that Miller’s representatives previously provided documentation showing that several allegations involving his daughter had been investigated by the Cuyahoga County Division of Children and Family Services and deemed unsubstantiated.

Emily Moreno has offered a sharply different account in court and to police. Her allegations include claims that Miller scalded, hit and threatened her during their marriage.

"It is shameful that Max Miller decided to go on a bizarre and lie-filled rant about his ex-wife to desperately try to save his political career," Emily Moreno spokesman Stefan Mychajliw wrote in a statement Sunday.

"There is a documented trove of evidence that Miller has a history of violent and dangerous behavior and no amount of victim shaming will change that. 

"It is despicable and abhorrent that Miller lied on an unhinged and humiliating video for their daughter to watch one day. 

"No loving parent would have ever used their daughter as a PR pawn to save their own political career. Miller can lie and spin on X, but he cannot do so under oath in a court of law. We are confident that justice will prevail in court."

The former couple finalized their divorce last year but remain engaged in litigation involving custody and defamation claims. Last week, Moreno’s lawyers asked a judge for an order restricting Miller’s contact with one of her attorneys, alleging that Miller had shouted at and physically grabbed the lawyer. Miller’s attorney did not respond to an Associated Press request for comment on that filing.

Miller has sued Moreno for defamation, contending that she has engaged in a pattern of false accusations intended to hurt his reputation and gain leverage in their legal dispute.

He also faces renewed litigation involving former White House press secretary Stephanie Grisham, a former girlfriend who previously accused him of physical abuse. Miller denied those allegations and sued Grisham for defamation before the two sides reached a confidential settlement. Grisham filed a new lawsuit in July accusing Miller of violating the settlement’s terms.

The controversy has increasingly spilled into Miller’s race for Ohio’s 7th Congressional District. Democrats have called for a House Ethics Committee investigation, and Rep. Shontel Brown, D-Ohio, has said Miller should resign. Poindexter said the allegations should receive the attention of law enforcement.

"No one credibly accused of holding a gun to his wife's head and breaking their 2-year-old daughter's collarbone belongs in the halls of power," Poindexter wrote in a statement after the X livestream.

The district remains Republican-leaning, but Miller won it with just over 51% of the vote in 2024. Democratic campaign organizations have said they are monitoring the race as they search for opportunities to expand the battleground in their effort to win control of the House.

Miller used the final portion of his address to attack what he described as reckless coverage and urged reporters to review documents and evidence.

"What has been especially disappointing is the role much of the media has played: Too many reporters accepted accusations as fact before examining the evidence, too many stories were written with a predetermined conclusion," Miller said.

"Journalism is supposed to ask difficult questions of everybody. Journalism is supposed to examine the evidence, challenge assumptions, and tell the whole story, not just the parts that generate the most clicks for all of you to reinforce a preferred narrative that only benefits you and destroys others throughout our country.

"And make no mistake whatsoever, that at the end of the day, we will continue to hold strong, clear our name."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Buffalo Bills moved on from Sean McDermott but their offseason moves won't be enough for a title
item.description: The Buffalo Bills hired Joe Brady and added DJ Moore and Bradley Chubb, but questions remain about whether Josh Allen can finally reach the Super Bowl.
item.content:encoded:
At what point do you give up on a team? When do you say "enough is enough" and make the decision to just believe it won’t happen for a squad?

I’m at that point personally, as I can’t support the Buffalo Bills winning a Super Bowl anymore. Last season had virtually everything break correctly for them, and they couldn’t get it done, so why do we think they will this year?

As mentioned, they didn’t win the Super Bowl, and they actually lost a playoff game in yet another heartbreaking fashion. The regular season was… odd. They started with four straight wins and looked dominant. They came back in a thriller to open the year and win 41-40 over the Ravens. Then they lost back-to-back weeks to the Patriots (who turned out to be very good) and the terrible Falcons. Their other losses came against the Dolphins, Texans, and Eagles. The Dolphins and Falcons were the only two-score losses they had during the year. They struggled to beat the Jaguars, then lost in overtime to the Broncos.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

I think the team also said they’ve had enough as they finally moved on from Sean McDermott. I don’t think you can really blame McDermott for everything, but sometimes you do need to switch it up and get rid of the coach. They hired Joe Brady, who is more offense-focused, and I’m not sure that was their major problem. They added DJ Moore to the team, and he might have his best seasons behind him. They added another guy who might have his best behind him in Bradley Chubb as well.

JOSH ALLEN SAYS HE WOULD BE 'VERY HONORED' TO PLAY FOR TEAM USA IN FLAG FOOTBALL AT 2028 OLYMPICS

A team that probably could use help on defense doesn’t seem to have done much to address the issue. The best defense for the team is keeping Josh Allen on the field, I guess. Allen is still elite and will keep the Bills relevant no matter what the rest of their unit looks like. It just feels like this team is being pieced together with randomness instead of a full plan. I want to see them start making moves that will push them ahead, not just keep them winning double-digits and relying on luck and Allen’s magic in the postseason.

I think the Patriots take a bit of a step back, as mentioned, but I really don’t see that happening with Allen under center for the Bills. They still have a tough schedule, but 10 wins does feel like the floor for this team every year, right? They’ve had 11 wins or more every year since 2020. I don’t see that changing here. I think a fun bet for them this year is over 4.5 division wins. I think they split with the Patriots, and they should sweep the Jets and Dolphins which gives you five wins. Since 2020, they have gotten five or more division wins three times. It is +115, so I like that look for them as well.

item.title: 'Remember the Titans' star Ethan Suplee issues warning about weight-loss drug craze
item.description: Ethan Suplee warns GLP-1 weight-loss drugs aren't a "one-stop shop," saying resistance training and healthy habits are essential for lasting results.
item.content:encoded:
Ethan Suplee pumped the brakes on the GLP-1 craze, warning that the wildly popular weight-loss drugs aren't the miracle fix many people believe they are.

As millions of Americans continue turning to blockbuster GLP-1 medications, Suplee said the drugs are only one piece of the puzzle. Drawing from his own decades-long weight-loss journey, the actor said sustainable success comes from building healthier habits instead of relying on medication alone.

Suplee has been candid about his decades-long battle with obesity. The "Remember the Titans" actor weighed roughly 500 pounds at his heaviest and ultimately lost around 300 pounds through years of diet and lifestyle changes. He has also undergone multiple skin-removal surgeries and now hosts weekly discussions on his show, "LifeLONG with Ethan Suplee," about long-term weight management.

MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS

The 50-year-old actor started dieting at just 5 years old and later, by his own volition, at age 24. "And I kind of spun my wheels for 15 years on these yo-yo diets simply because I didn't communicate," Suplee told Fox News Digital. "And when I didn't communicate to anyone else, I didn't actually figure out what I really wanted."

After decades of trial and error, Suplee said his own experience taught him there isn't a shortcut to lasting weight loss. While he acknowledged the weight-loss drugs can be an effective tool, he argued they aren't a replacement for building healthier habits.

"As a kid, I wanted a magical diet drug so badly. And now we have what is a magical diet drug," he said. "I think, unfortunately, it's also not a one-stop shop. I think you can hop on a GLP-1 and experience weight loss. You can see the scale go down week over week for a long time without having to do anything else."

"... I think when people imagine their ideal — I don't think the GLP-1s get anyone to their ideal."

'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SHOWS OFF MUSCLES AFTER DRASTIC WEIGHT LOSS TRANSFORMATION

Suplee emphasized that the medications can dramatically improve people's health and said he wouldn't discourage anyone from using them.

"By the way, a small amount of weight loss provides a huge health benefit," he added. "So if you're just going into it, going like, 'I just want to be healthier. Let me hop on this GLP-1 agonist and improve my health.' Bravo to you. You're going to do that... I'm not criticizing those people."

But Suplee said the conversation becomes more nuanced for people hoping to reach an "ideal" weight or transform their physique.

"I think for those people, just hopping on a GLP-1 is not enough," Suplee added. "I think it also will require some resistance training to preserve lean tissue... maybe increase protein a bit... I just think [they] aren't a one-stop shop."

WATCH: ‘REMEMBER THE TITANS’ STAR ETHAN SUPLEE WARNS POPULAR GLP-1 DRUGS AREN'T A CURE-ALL FOR LASTING WEIGHT LOSS

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The "My Name is Earl" star said his own experience ultimately shaped a simple philosophy: There's no single answer when it comes to long-term weight loss. He said lasting success comes from addressing the many factors that influence a person's health and relationship with food.

"I don't think it's ever going to be one thing," Suplee explained. "I think it is partially the amount of food you're consuming, partially the types of food you're consuming, partially how sedentary you are, and partially your emotional and potentially mental behavior and relationship with food."

"There's an ecosystem to everybody's life."

It's a lesson Suplee said became even clearer after he reached his goal weight.

"I found maintaining weight loss to be a hell of a lot harder and more complicated than losing weight," he admitted.

Suplee said he still grapples with the same cravings he experienced before losing roughly 300 pounds.

"If I see an advertisement for McDonald's, I want McDonald's," he said. "I'm hungry. This is true today as it was 20 years ago."

WATCH: ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS WEIGHT LOSS WOULD BRING NEW EDGE TO ROLE HE'D LOVE TO REVISIT

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

He was quick to clarify that long-term weight maintenance isn't about completely cutting out fast food, including McDonald's.

"But it's not eating it emotionally, not eating it to cure my anxiety, not eating it out of compulsion, and then not overeating it," Suplee added. "Like, these are all the factors I have to deal with to maintain my weight."

When asked what has allowed him to maintain his weight loss over the years, Suplee pointed to a less obvious factor: learning to be honest with himself by opening up to others.

"I found I could become more honest with myself by opening up and being honest with other people," Suplee said. "And I think that really made a huge difference in my ability to maintain this weight loss as long as I have."

item.title: Ancient Book of Revelation city gives up stunning secret buried for 1,500 years
item.description: A 1,500-year-old geometric mosaic with a heart-shaped ivy leaf was uncovered in ancient Smyrna, one of the seven churches in the Book of Revelation.
item.content:encoded:
An ancient mosaic was recently revealed in a Turkish city long known for being one of the seven churches mentioned in the Book of Revelation.

The artwork was uncovered in the ancient city of Smyrna, an archaeological site in modern-day İzmir, Turkey, according to Turkish state news outlet Anadolu Agency (AA).

Smyrna — along with Ephesus, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea — is one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed by Jesus in the Book of Revelation.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNEARTH ANCIENT TREASURE CACHE AT BIBLICAL CITY CONNECTED TO GENESIS

Revelation 2:8 states: "To the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of him who is the First and the Last, who died and came to life again."

The mosaic was found during infrastructure work at the archaeological site. It dates to between the fourth and sixth centuries A.D., according to officials, and measures roughly 16.4 by 8.2 feet.

Photos show archaeologists brushing away centuries of dirt to reveal the remarkably preserved 1,500-year-old mosaic and its geometric and floral motifs.

Excavation director Akın Ersoy said the mosaic was first found last year, but archaeologists did not fully excavate the artwork until this year, according to AA.

LOST SERMONS FROM ONE OF CHRISTIANITY'S GREATEST SAINTS DISCOVERED AFTER 1,600 YEARS

"In connection with this, we also found traces of the walls that defined the space," said Ersoy.

"We believe that a structure was built over the mosaic during the Ottoman period in the 19th century, and that the new layout was created while avoiding damage to the mosaic floor as much as possible."

The most striking motif is the heart-shaped ivy leaf, which is made of red tesserae, or mosaic tiles.

Though modern people see the heart as a symbol of love, Ersoy said the mosaic was created long before the symbol came to represent romance.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It was not very clear in the early periods that the heart represented affection and love. We see the heart emerge as a symbol of love in paintings during the Renaissance," he said.

Rather, Ersoy said the heart-shaped ivy leaf was intended to symbolize loyalty.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The ivy leaf clings to trees and walls," he said. "It came to symbolize loyalty and has been used from antiquity through the centuries."

Archaeologists also uncovered bags, cooking pots and earthenware vessels dating to the late Ottoman Empire and the early years of the Turkish Republic, suggesting the space was reused roughly 1,500 years after the mosaic was laid.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"We can say that the people of that period consciously protected it because there is very little damage," the archaeologist said.

"The space was brought back to life after 1,500 years."

The latest discovery is one of several recent archaeological finds in cities mentioned in the Book of Revelation.

Last summer, archaeologists uncovered a massive Roman council hall in Laodicea, which featured carvings linked to early Christian worship.

Months later, archaeologists announced the discovery of a Roman-era marble bathtub and other ancient artifacts in Ephesus.

item.title: Southern university requires business suits, bans du-rags and other headwear in new dress code
item.description: Tuskegee University's new dress code bans du-rags, bonnets and sagging pants in classrooms as part of its broader workforce readiness push.
item.content:encoded:
Retired U.S. Air Force Maj. Gen. Dr. Mark Brown, president and CEO of Tuskegee University in Alabama, is bringing forward a "professional educational environment" to one of the nation's most prestigious Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU).

Students will be required to bring a business suit and shoes to campus for business-like meetings and cannot dress unprofessionally in the classrooms or cafeterias. Head coverings will also be barred, with exceptions for those that serve religious or medical purposes.

"The university has developed a new policy for student attire on campus, classroom attendance, and cell phone use in classrooms," Brown wrote in a message to students. "Tuskegee students now have a dress code for public and professional places."

"The Student Handbook requires students to arrive on campus with a business suit and proper shoes for a business meeting," the message said. "Students are prohibited from wearing revealing clothing in class, to the cafeteria or in official settings like Convocation. They are also not able to wear bedroom shoes, bonnets, or du-rags to class or the cafeteria."

MICHELLE OBAMA ACCUSES MEDIA OF WEAPONIZING FASHION TO 'DIMINISH' HER AS A CAMPAIGN THREAT

The Alabama school is also restricting revealing and sexually explicit clothing as part of a broader push to prepare college students for the workforce.

"The goal here is not meant to restrict you from enjoying the Tuskegee Experience, but to prepare you with a solid foundation for the workforce you will enter once you leave Tuskegee," Brown, who took over as Tuskegee University president two years ago, wrote. "Employers are less forgiving and too often presentation may overrule stellar preparation.

"Tuskegee University continues to prepare the best and brightest for a lifetime of success," Brown added. "With these changes, we want to ensure every student is as prepared as they can be. I look forward to seeing you in August."

Tuskegee’s fall orientation guidance lists business attire for career fairs, meetings, interviews and other professional occasions, but the guidance does restrict unprofessional attire in classrooms, too.

"Hats, bonnets, head scarves, caps, hoods, du-rags, bandanas, sunglasses, and other non-religious or non-medically required head coverings should be removed while in the classroom or cafeteria unless they are required for documented medical, religious, cultural, or University-approved purposes," the Dress Code Policy for Students that accompanied Brown's message read.

"Pants, skirts, dresses, and shorts should be worn in a manner that is appropriate for a professional educational environment. Clothing should fit properly and not expose undergarments or other private areas. Excessively short shorts, swimsuit bottoms, body suits, sleeveless undershirts, and similar casual garments are not appropriate for professional classroom settings," the guidance continued. "T-shirts worn as dresses and sagging pants are not permitted. Baggy or loose fitting pants must be worn with a belt that fits around the waist."

Faculty members will be authorized to respond when students are dressed in violation of the guidelines, though the president’s message did not specify potential penalties.

Some elements of the announcement reinforce standards that were already on the books. Tuskegee’s 2025-26 student handbook required students to dress "in good taste," prohibited sleepwear outside residence halls and barred men from wearing "do rags," stocking caps, bandanas, baseball caps and other headwear inside university buildings. It also prohibited sagging pants in academic facilities.

The revised rules have fueled a wider debate over professionalism, cultural expression and the expectations placed on students at HBCUs. Critics online have described restrictions on du-rags and bonnets as respectability politics that unfairly target clothing associated with Black culture.

Supporters argue that colleges should teach students how to present themselves during interviews, meetings and other professional situations.

Several alumni have defended the university’s approach. Tuskegee graduate Gwen McKinney told NBC4 Washington that the policy was "a breath of fresh air," saying there is "a time and place and a setting for every kind of dress."

"A critical part of being ready for and confident in business environments is being appropriately dressed," Walter P. Cooper Sr., director of the Career Education and Leadership Development Center, said.

"We know that every workplace doesn’t require business attire – our center includes business casual and casual attire, too – but as our students prepare to enter those workplace scenarios that do, it is important that access to the right wardrobe is not a barrier."

For students that might not have the proper attire, there is The Golden Tigers Community Closet to help outfit needy students.

"One of the key pillars of Tuskegee’s Renaissance Era is our focus on career readiness for our students," Brown said. "Academically, we are equipping our students to stand shoulder to shoulder with any candidates competing for roles in the global economy.

"The Golden Tigers Community Closet is an important way to ensure that every student can also feel confidently dressed when they step into those spaces."

The dress code is part of a larger set of classroom and career-readiness rules being introduced as Tuskegee expects its highest new-student enrollment in 32 years. Cellphone use will be prohibited unless authorized by an instructor.

"Faculty will be empowered to respond to students who are inappropriately dressed based on these guidelines," Brown's message to students added.

"Faculty will also be able to respond to a different classroom challenge – cell phones. Unless directed by the professor, students are no longer allowed to use their cell phones while in class. They should be turned off to eliminate any distraction from the instructor’s lesson."
